findings.summary: AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync lets a launcher exception (the real ProcessLauncher throws what Process.Start throws, ProcessLauncher.cs:267) escape, and AfterRoundAsync's catch-all (QuotaCooldownRound.cs:52) then drops every key's decision for the round, so a spent agy refusal that should park on stated/guess parks nothing and the round's Claude/Codex parks and Ok lifts are lost too.
findings.fix: Catch non-cancellation exceptions in ReadAsync and return AgyQuotaRead.CannotCheck(why); test first: a launcher fake that throws Win32Exception for the /quota launch, with one agy row ended RateLimited (AGY_1_3_3, Spent true) and one codex row ended hopeless, expecting Standing('antigravity/gemini').Source == 'stated' and a standing codex entry (red today: both null).

findings.summary: Parse reads one line per AGY_ERROR, so the issue's own stderr sample (plan section 1, the six-line AGY_ERROR block) yields no error, and AntigravityRuntime.RateLimited then falls to ByText with Spent null, leaving the explicit Individual quota reached refusal undecided and parked only if the /quota gauge reads spent.
findings.fix: Parse the balanced JSON object that follows the marker across the following lines (RESULTS 3.1 captured the one-line form, so the multi-line form must be settled with the owner and written into D2); test first: AgyError.Parse over the plan's multi-line block returns one error with IsSpentQuota true and AntigravityRuntime.RateLimited gives Spent == true (red today: empty list).

findings.summary: The consult failure labels a RateLimited outcome by RateLimit.Hopeless(r.Reason) and ignores Spent, so a Claude spend-limit verdict (Spent true, sentence 'You've hit your monthly spend limit… (HTTP 429)', which matches no RateLimit.Spent phrase at ReviewerExecutor.cs:369) becomes ConsultFailure.RateLimited with transient wording.
findings.fix: Use r.Spent ?? RateLimit.Hopeless(r.Reason) at that line; test first: a consult whose Claude launch is the spend envelope expects ConsultFailure.Quota (red today: RateLimited).

findings.summary: QuotaKeyOf sees only the model, yet RosterBuilder.SettingsFor (RosterBuilder.cs:531) gives every CLI row its vault key as ApiKey and KeyEnv/ClaudeRuntime.cs:112 then run the CLI on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, a different account and quota: a spent API-key row parks the shared 'claude' or 'codex' key and excludes the sign-in rows that still have quota, and the reverse.
findings.fix: Key the quota by credential mode as well (the row's settings or Request.Environment, not the row id), so an API-key row and a sign-in row never share a key; test first: two Claude rows, one with ApiKey set and one without, the API one ends RateLimited spend-limit, expecting Standing('claude') null and the sign-in row not excluded (red today: the sign-in row is excluded).

findings.summary: The rounds block still draws the ledger's reset line (resetHint of cardResetLine) for a provider that has a cooldown standing, so a cooling row can show two lines about one reset where D9 says the cooldown line replaces the reset line.
findings.fix: Decide whether the round's history line is meant to stay; if not, pass the standing cooldown into roundsBlock and draw cooldownLine instead of resetHint; test first: a roundsBlock over a cooling provider with a roundsSnapshot reset expects no reset hint (red today: the hint is drawn).

findings.summary: A transient RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with no sentence gets Spent null, and 'exhausted' is a spent word, so BoundedScheduler.Hopeless (BoundedScheduler.cs:681) stops after one launch; plan section 5 story 1 says the transient RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED climbs the ladder, and S2 tests only Spent false, which agy never produces.
findings.fix: Settle with the owner whether this case climbs or stops and align section 5 with D2 or the code; if it must climb, test first: exit 3 with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 429): too many requests expects 4 launches (red today: 1).
